With a blossoming career, Eru has collaborated with icons like Adele, Demi Lovato, Nathan Pacheco and David Archuleta, earning a Grammy nomination. She's also a TEDx speaker, Keynote presenter at Lawrence University, and a musical director at Harvard.
Eru has performed with symphonies all over the world including the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra in London, Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra in Tokyo, the Hawaii Symphony in Honolulu, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra in Shanghai, the Düsseldorfer Symphoniker, and the New York City Ballet among many other venerable institutions. She has also regularly performed as guest soloist at celebrated venues such as Avery Fisher Hall, Lincoln Center, Carnegie Hall, Walt Disney Concert Hall, Wembley Arena, Mitsubishi Electric Halle, Neal S. Blaisdell Center, Adrienne Arsht Center and Shanghai Symphony Hall.
Furthermore, Eru performed at the Grand Finals at DOTA 2 in Seattle, has made an appearance with Skrillex and Chance the Rapper on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and was invited to be a Guest of Honor two years in a row at Anime Expo alongside legendary rock band KISS. She co-hosted a TV Documentary program on Chopin filmed in Warsaw, Poland in the The Łazienki Palace. She is featured on numerous video game soundtracks, including Sony’s popular franchise, Everquest. Eru is also a member of symphonic rock band Critical Hit which tours the US and Europe. 
Prepare to fall in love with the enchanting cello sound of Eru as she performs timeless Disney pieces alongside Van Anh Nguyen and Jules Aurora at the Summer Expo on July 16th.

Join Jules Aurora at the Summer Expo on July 16th for an enchanting performance of timeless Disney soundtracks. Experience the magic as she sings beloved songs from Aladdin, The Little Mermaid, Beauty & The Beast, Pocahontas, and more. Don't miss out on this captivating musical journey!

With a Sydney Opera House debut at the age of 8, Van-Anh's infectious personality and emotive playing have enchanted audiences across renowned venues worldwide. From the Sydney Opera House to the Forbidden City Concert Hall and the Segerstrom Performing Arts Center, her talent shines brightly. She collaborates with esteemed orchestras such as the Ho Chi Minh City Symphony Orchestra and the Vietnamese American Philharmonic Orchestra.
Van-Anh's versatility extends beyond classical performances, as she brings creative classical-crossover arrangements and mash-ups to stages, captivating brands like Moet & Chandon, Tiffany & Co, and Porsche. With 10 albums released on major digital music platforms, including a recent release on Deutsche Grammophon, she has been featured in prestigious publications and even had her own TV show on Discovery Channel Asia.

Rolex has no shareholders. No quarterly earnings calls. No public reporting.

Since 1960, the company has been owned entirely by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation — a private nonprofit. Every profit stays inside. No dividends. No investors to answer to.

The result: over 1 million watches a year. $13 billion in annual revenue. And a brand that deliberately keeps supply below demand to protect its value. ⏱️

Most luxury companies are optimizing for growth. Rolex is optimizing for scarcity, quality, and staying exactly where it is — permanently out of reach for most people.

Taxes affect money at nearly every stage of its life cycle, making them one of the biggest factors in personal finance.

The American Revolution was sparked in part by opposition to British taxes, with the rallying cry “No taxation without representation.” More than two centuries later, taxation remains one of the most debated topics in economics and politics. Today, people may pay taxes when they earn income, buy goods and services, own property, sell investments for a profit, or transfer wealth through certain estates, depending on the laws in their country and jurisdiction.

Taxes help fund public services such as roads, schools, healthcare, emergency services, and national defense, but there is ongoing debate about how much should be collected and how those funds should be used.

This Is How Much Money The U.S. Owes To Other Countries.

The United States holds one of the world’s largest national debts, and a significant portion is owned by foreign governments and investors. Countries such as Japan, China, and the United Kingdom are among the largest foreign holders of U.S. Treasury securities, investing in them because they are widely considered one of the safest financial assets in the world.

Owning U.S. debt doesn’t mean these countries “control” the United States—it means they’ve invested in U.S. government bonds and earn interest over time. Swipe through to see which countries hold the most U.S. debt and what those investments reveal about the global economy.

Theresa Dallavale arrives from the bigger firm, takes over Erin Brockovich's files, and calls them a great start with a few holes to fill. Politely, which somehow makes it worse.

Erin asks whose number she needs. Theresa says all of them, obviously, nobody memorizes 600 plaintiffs.

So Erin gives her one. Annabelle Daniels. Ten years old, eleven in May. The phone number. The pool she swam in every day because she wanted to be a synchronized swimmer. Her parents, Ted and Rita, and exactly what each of them is sick with. Her uncle's family down the road, all five kids by name, and their number too.

Theresa was right that a lawsuit needs contact details in a file. She was just wrong about where the information was living.

Erin had spent 18 months at kitchen tables in Hinkley. She wasn't collecting data, she was collecting people, and people tell you things no form ever asks for.

These Are The Top 5 Monthly Money Machines:

If waiting three months for quarterly dividends feels like watching paint dry, monthly dividend assets offer the ultimate instant gratification. Real estate giant Realty Income ($O)—literally nicknamed “The Monthly Dividend Company”—has paid over 650 consecutive monthly dividends while maintaining a steady ~5.1% yield. Premier business development firm Main Street Capital ($MAIN) cranks out monthly cash alongside $0.30 supplemental dividends, pushing its effective yield near 6%. The psychological rush of watching cash hit your account 12 times a year makes these tickers a favorite for income-focused investors.

This monthly cash machine sparks an intense battle between yield-obsessed investors and cautious wealth managers. Morningstar analyst David Swartz actively warn that chasing double-digit monthly payouts often hides net asset value erosion and imminent dividend cuts. Conversely, dividend growth bulls argue that well-managed monthly payers offer unmatched compounding speed and liquidity. Chasing risky 15%+ yields is pure recklessness, but dismissing quality monthly income is equally foolish. Investors seeking dependable recurring cash should keep an eye on BDC leader Main Street Capital ($MAIN) and retail property king Agree Realty ($ADC) as top growth-and-income stocks to watch.

In this video, a man uses small rectangular blocks laid out on a black board to demonstrate the butterfly effect. One tiny push starts a chain reaction that grows larger and larger with every step.

At first, the movement looks insignificant. One block falls into another. Then another. And before you realize it, the entire system is shifting because of a single small action.

It shows how the biggest outcomes rarely begin with big moves. They begin with something so small that most people would ignore it.

One decision.
One habit.
One choice repeated over time.
That is how everything changes.

The butterfly effect is simple but uncomfortable. You never really know which small action will rewrite the future. You only know that nothing stays small forever.

In April 2018, Elon Musk sent every Tesla employee an email that has been passed around offices ever since.

Most of it was about factory upgrades during the Model 3 crunch, but the final section was a short list of productivity rules that ended up outliving everything else in the message.

- Cut the large meetings unless everyone in the room is getting something out of them, and stop the recurring ones once the urgent problem is actually solved.

- Walk out the moment you realize you are no longer contributing, because sitting quietly in a room where you add nothing helps nobody.

- Drop the internal acronyms, and talk directly to whoever can solve the problem instead of pushing it up through layers of managers first.

Almost none of it is complicated, which is probably why people still share it years later.

Bạn từng bị nghi ngờ? Hãy bước mạnh hơn.
Bạn từng nghĩ mình tầm thường? Đây là lúc để bước khác biệt.
Quan trọng không phải là bạn đến từ đâu, mà là bạn muốn đi đến đâu. Cuối năm này, hãy cho bản thân một lời hứa, không phải để thay đổi mọi thứ, mà là để chính bạn thay đổi cách nhìn về mình.
